# Private–Public Gap (Anonymous Companion Repository)

Companion repository for an **anonymous submission under review**.

This repository holds the full prompt templates and lexical audit
referenced in the manuscript, so reviewers and readers can reproduce,
audit, or build on the simulation without having to reverse-engineer it
from the manuscript text.

> *Author names, affiliations, and full citation will be added upon
> acceptance.*

---

## Why this repo exists

A central methodological commitment of the paper is the
**Non-Circular Prompting Protocol**: agents are prompted with universal
psychological principles (impression management, interpersonal risk,
trust) rather than with the target outcome. To make that claim auditable
we publish every prompt verbatim. If a reader believes a prompt encodes
the result we report, they can show *which sentence* and *how*; we treat
that openness as part of the contribution.

---

## Repository layout

```
private-public-gap/
├── README.md                       ← you are here
├── prompts/
│   ├── 01_private_belief.md        ← AGENT_INTERNAL_UPDATE
│   ├── 02_public_statement.md      ← AGENT_SAFETY_FILTER_MAIN  (core mechanism)
│   ├── 03_phase_judges.md          ← PHASE_TRANSITION_CHECK + PHASE_VIOLATION_CHECK
│   ├── 04_consensus_judges.md      ← CONSENSUS_CHECK + OBSERVER_CONSENSUS_QUALITY
│   └── 05_intervention.md          ← INTERVENTION_GENERATION (optional, not used in main results)
├── code/
│   ├── src/                        ← simulator core (CognitiveAgent, PhasedRoundTable, validation metrics, prompts)
│   ├── scripts/                    ← experiment runners (Exp 1–4, ablation, dynamics) and analysis utilities
│   └── requirements.txt            ← Python dependencies
└── data/
    ├── exp1_teams/                 ← per-turn private/public transcripts for all 210 Experiment 1 teams
    ├── exp1_main_summary.json      ← team-level summary statistics for Experiment 1
    ├── exp4_dynamics_main.json     ← per-team episode trajectories for Experiment 4 (longitudinal)
    └── llm_judge_cache.json        ← FULL/PARTIAL/OMITTED disclosure judgements (per private–public pair)
```

To reproduce a single experiment:
```
pip install -r code/requirements.txt
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...   # and/or GEMINI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
python code/scripts/experiments/run_experiment_1_main.py --model gpt-5-mini --teams-per-n 30
python code/scripts/experiments/run_experiment_5_dynamics.py --model gpt-5-mini --teams-per-regime 15 --n-episodes 6
```

Each `prompts/*.md` file gives the prompt verbatim, the input variables
it expects, and a short explanation of where it sits in the simulation
pipeline. Each `data/exp1_teams/team_NNNN.txt` reproduces the
per-agent-per-turn private statement, public statement, phase, and
consensus state for one of the 210 teams; combined with the judge
cache, the statement-level numbers reported in §4.3 of the manuscript
can be recomputed exactly.

---

## How prompts map to the manuscript

| Manuscript section | Prompt(s) used | What it produces |
|---|---|---|
| Dual-Process Agent Design | `01_private_belief.md` | Private Belief — what the agent thinks |
| Cognitive Process Tracing | `02_public_statement.md` | Public Statement + self-classified disclosure level |
| Discussion Protocol (three phases) | `03_phase_judges.md` | Phase pacing decisions (controller-level only) |
| Measurement / Consensus Turn | `04_consensus_judges.md` | When the team reached agreement, and whether that agreement was genuine |
| Active observer (extension, not in main results) | `05_intervention.md` | Intervention message when fake consensus is detected |

The reversal experiment reported in the manuscript varies the framing
inside `02_public_statement.md`; every other prompt is held constant.

---

## Reproducing the main numbers

The manuscript reports four numerical anchors that depend directly on
these prompts:

- **Trust–disclosure correlation**: design-level Pearson *r* = +0.88
  across six stratification bins; team-level Spearman *ρ* = +0.23
  (*p* < .001, *n* = 210 teams, GPT-5-mini); individual-level
  OR = 3.02 across 9,291 agent–statement pairs
- **Reversal-frame correlation** *r* = −0.26 (n = 90 teams)
- **Faction-trust observation bias**:
  ~44 → ~5 hidden items as inter-faction trust moves 1 → 5
  (n = 540 teams primary; 1,263 teams pooled with high-resolution
  supplementary runs)
- **Within-topic correlations** Spearman *ρ* ranging from +0.16 to
  +0.48 across the five scenario archetypes (positive in all five)

If you re-run the prompts in this repo against a current frontier model
and obtain a meaningfully different sign or magnitude, please open an
issue — that is exactly the kind of finding we would want to know about.
